meanings.usage: 常与介词to搭配，表示“对某人来说难以到达/获取”
可用来形容人、地方或风俗，常与介词to搭配
常与介词to/towards搭配，表示“对……怀有敌意”

meanings.meaning: 周围地区，邻近区域（常用搭配in the vicinity (of) 表示“在（……的）附近”）

meanings.usage: 常与介词on/upon搭配，指大量人突然涌入某个地方
指长时间费力地步行，常接表示地点的介词短语
指用船将人、货物运到河或海峡的对岸，常用搭配ferry sb/sth across sth
常用被动形式be perched on/upon，指建筑物位于高处或边缘位置
用来形容道路、村落等分布零散、不整齐的状态
形容地方、外表等看起来吓人、不友好

meanings.meaning: 破烂不堪的，年久失修的
meanings.usage: 用来形容建筑物、家具等因缺乏维护而破旧的状态
指人或物排成的长队，a procession of 表示“一队……”
常与介词at搭配，表示愤怒地盯着某人看
常与介词at/through/into搭配，指因看不清而仔细凝视

phrases.usage: 表示“与……隔绝，切断与……的联系”，被动形式be cut off from更常用

examples.en: The small village is cut off from the outside world in winter due to heavy snow.
examples.zh: 冬天大雪封山，这个小村庄与外界隔绝了。

phrases.usage: 表示“在附近，在邻近地区”，后可接of+具体地点说明范围

examples.en: There are several famous scenic spots in the vicinity of the hotel.
examples.zh: 酒店附近有好几处著名景点。

phrases.usage: 指“（大量人）突然到访，涌入”，带有出人意料、给当地带来压力的含义

examples.en: Every summer, crowds of tourists descend on this coastal town.
examples.zh: 每年夏天，大批游客涌入这个海滨小镇。

phrases.usage: 口语常用表达，意思是“不知道，不清楚”，后可接疑问词引导的从句

examples.en: I have no idea when he will come back from his business trip.
examples.zh: 我不知道他什么时候出差回来。

phrases.usage: 表示“睡得很熟，酣睡”，是固定搭配，fast此处为副词，修饰asleep

examples.en: When I got home last night, my kids were already fast asleep in bed.
examples.zh: 我昨晚到家的时候，孩子们已经在床上睡得很熟了。

phrases.usage: 表示“害怕……，对……感到腼腆/迟疑”，后接名词或动名词

examples.en: Many children are shy of speaking in front of a large audience.
examples.zh: 很多孩子都不好意思在很多人面前讲话。

phrases.usage: 表示“苏醒过来，恢复生机，变得活跃”，可用于描述人、地方或场景

examples.en: The quiet park comes to life at dawn when elderly people come to do exercise.
examples.zh: 清晨老人们来锻炼的时候，安静的公园就变得热闹起来。

phrases.usage: 固定句型，意思是“毫无疑问……”，that引导同位语从句说明doubt的内容

examples.en: There is no doubt that regular exercise is good for physical and mental health.
examples.zh: 毫无疑问，规律锻炼对身心健康都有好处。

grammar.title: 独立主格结构
grammar.structure: 名词/代词 + 现在分词/过去分词/形容词/副词/介词短语
grammar.definition: 由名词/代词 + 非谓语动词/形容词/副词/介词短语构成，在句中作状语，说明时间、原因、条件、伴随情况等，其逻辑主语与主句主语不一致 多用于书面语，可使句子结构更紧凑，避免重复使用从句

examples.en: The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
examples.zh: 村庄似乎已经废弃了，唯一的生命迹象是一头样子难看的黑山羊，用短绳拴在附近地里的一棵树上。

examples.en: The meeting over, everyone went home tired but satisfied.
examples.zh: 会议结束了，每个人都疲惫但满足地回家了。

grammar.title: as引导的非限制性定语从句
grammar.structure: 主句 + as + 定语从句 / As + 定语从句, 主句
grammar.definition: as可用来引导非限制性定语从句，指代整个主句的内容，可位于主句之前、之后或插入主句中间，常译为“正如……，正像……” 常用于引出已发生的事实、大家已知的情况等，常见搭配有as we all know, as is expected, as is mentioned above等

examples.en: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable--as my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
examples.zh: 到真正偏僻的村庄去旅游很少是愉快的——我和妻子在巴尔干半岛旅行时就发现了这一点。

examples.en: As is known to all, the earth moves around the sun.
examples.zh: 众所周知，地球绕着太阳转。

original.en: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
original.zh: 这些教堂吸引了很多游客，因为它们不仅具有很高的建筑价值，而且还藏有大量保存完好的壁画。

imitations.en: The book is very popular, for it is not only educational, but very interesting as well.
imitations.zh: 这本书很受欢迎，因为它不仅有教育意义，而且还非常有趣。

imitations.en: The new shopping mall is convenient, for it not only has a wide range of goods, but offers excellent customer service as well.
imitations.zh: 这个新购物中心很方便，因为它不仅商品种类齐全，而且还提供优质的客户服务。

original.en: We expected the path to end abruptly, but we found that it traced its way through the trees.
original.zh: 我们原以为小路会突然到头，却发现它在树林中蜿蜒延伸。

imitations.en: We expected the exam to be very difficult, but we found that it was much easier than we had imagined.
imitations.zh: 我们原以为考试会很难，却发现它比我们想象的容易得多。

imitations.en: We expected the restaurant to be crowded, but we found that there were still plenty of empty tables.
imitations.zh: 我们原以为这家餐厅会很拥挤，却发现还有很多空桌。

patterns.pattern: The most frightening/annoying/exciting thing of all was that...

original.en: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
original.zh: 最吓人的是，这里听不到一点声音。

imitations.en: The most annoying thing of all was that he didn't even apologize for his mistake.
imitations.zh: 最气人的是，他甚至都没有为自己的错误道歉。

imitations.en: The most exciting thing of all was that our team won the first prize in the competition.
imitations.zh: 最令人激动的是，我们队在比赛中获得了一等奖。

lines.en: In this much-travelled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.
lines.zh: 在这个旅游频繁的世界上，仍有成千上万个游人足迹未至的地方。

lines.en: We always assume that villagers in remote places are friendly and hospitable .
lines.zh: 人们总是以为偏僻的地方的村民们热情好客。

lines.en: But people who are cut off not only from foreign tourists, but even from their own countrymen can be hostile to travellers.
lines.zh: 但是，那些不但与外国旅游者隔绝，而且与本国同胞隔绝的人们有可能对游客抱有敌意。

lines.en: Visits to really remote villages are seldom enjoyable -- as my wife and I discovered during a tour through the Balkans.
lines.zh: 到真正偏僻的村庄去旅游并不是一件愉快的事情。

lines.en: We had spent several days in a small town and visited a number of old churches in the vicinity.
lines.zh: 我与妻子在一次周游巴尔干半岛时对此深有体会。

lines.en: These attracted many visitors, for they were not only of great architectural interest, but contained a large number of beautifully preserved frescoes as well.
lines.zh: 我们在一座小镇上逗留了几天，参观了附近的许多古老的教堂。

lines.en: On the day before our departure, several bus loads of tourists descended on the town.
lines.zh: 这些教堂吸引大量游客，不仅是因为建筑风格奇特，而且还有大量保存完好的壁画。

lines.en: This was more than we could bear, so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside.
lines.zh: 我们离开小镇的前一天，镇上来了几辆满载游客的公共汽车。

lines.en: Taking a path which led out of the town, we crossed a few fields until we came to a dense wood.
lines.zh: 人多得使我们难以忍受，于是我们决定利用最后一天去乡间一游。

lines.en: We expected the path to end abruptly , but we found that it traced its way through the trees.
lines.zh: 我们走上了一条出镇的小路，穿过几块农田，来到一片茂密的树林。

lines.en: We tramped through the wood for over two hours until we arrived at a deep stream.
lines.zh: 我们原以为小路会到此突然终止。

lines.en: We could see that the path continued on the other side, but we had no idea how we could get across the stream.
lines.zh: 没想到它到树林中继续向前延伸。

lines.en: Suddenly my wife spotted a boat moored to the bank.
lines.zh: 我们在树林中跋涉了两个多小时，到了一条深溪边。

lines.en: In it there was a boatman fast asleep.
lines.zh: 我们可以看到小路在深溪对岸继续向前伸展，但却不知如何越过这道深溪。

lines.en: We gently woke him up and asked him to ferry us to the other side.
lines.zh: 突然，妻子发现岸边泊着一条小船，船上有一船夫在呼呼大睡。

lines.en: Though he was reluctant to do so at first, we eventually persuaded him to take us.
lines.zh: 我们轻轻地把他唤醒，请他把我们摆渡过溪。

lines.en: The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
lines.zh: 一开始，他很不愿意，但经劝说，终于同意了。

lines.en: The place consisted of a straggling unmade road which was lined on either side by small houses.
lines.zh: 顺着小路，我们来到一个座落在陡峭山坡上的小村庄。

lines.en: Even under a clear blue sky, the village looked forbidding, as all the houses were built of grey mud bricks.
lines.zh: 这儿有一条未经修筑的弯弯曲曲的道路，路两边排列着一些矮小的农舍。

lines.en: The village seemed deserted , the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
lines.zh: 农舍全用灰色的土坯建成，因此，即使在晴朗的蓝天底下，村庄看上去也会令人感到难以亲近。

lines.en: Sitting down on a dilapidated wooden fence near the field, we opened a couple of tins of sardines and had a picnic lunch.
lines.zh: 村里似乎无人居住，唯一的生命迹象是附近田里一只面目可憎的黑山羊，用一截短绳拴在一棵树上。

lines.en: All at once, I noticed that my wife seemed to be filled with alarm.
lines.zh: 我们在田边一堵东倒西歪的篱笆墙上坐下来，打开几听沙丁鱼罐头，吃了一顿野外午餐。

lines.en: Looking up I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently as we ate.
lines.zh: 突然，我注意到妻子十分惊恐。

lines.en: We offered them food and spoke to them kindly , but they remained motionless.
lines.zh: 我抬头一看，发现我们被一群衣衫褴褛的小孩团团围住了，他们在默不作声地看着我们吃饭。

lines.en: I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.
lines.zh: 我们给他们东西吃，客客气气地同他们交谈，但他们却一动也不动。

lines.en: When we later walked down the main street of the villager, we were followed by a silent procession of children.
lines.zh: 我认为这不过是他们在陌生人面前表现出的害羞。

lines.en: The village which had seemed deserted, immediately came to life.
lines.zh: 后来，我们在村里的主要街道上行走的时候，一队默不作声的孩子跟在我们后头。

lines.en: Faces appeared at windows. Men in shirt sleeves stood outside their houses and glared at us. Old women in black shawls peered at us from doorways .
lines.zh: 刚才还似乎空荡荡的村庄一下子活跃了起来，窗口露出了一张张面孔，只穿着衬衣的男人们站在屋子外面凶狠地盯着我们，披黑纱巾的老妇人站在门口偷偷地瞅着我们。

lines.en: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
lines.zh: 最令人害怕的是到处没有一点声音。

lines.en: There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.
lines.zh: 毫无疑问，我们的来访是不受欢迎的。

lines.en: We needed no further warning.
lines.zh: 我们不需要进一步的警告了。

lines.en: Turning back down the main street, we quickened our pace and made our way rapidly towards the stream where we hoped the boatman was waiting.
lines.zh: 便掉转身子，沿着那条主要街道加快步伐，快速地朝深溪边走去，希望船夫还在那儿等着我们。

questions.zh: 这个村庄为什么一片寂静？
questions.a: Because the villagers were hostile to the strangers: they watched the couple in complete silence and no one made a sound, so the couple realised they were unwelcome visitors and left.
questions.aZh: 因为村民对外来者怀有敌意：他们一声不响地注视着这对夫妇，全村听不到一点声音，夫妇俩于是意识到自己不受欢迎，便离开了。
questions.hint: 答案见 The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard. 与 There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors.

questions.q: What did the writer and his wife do on the last day of their stay in the small town?
questions.zh: 在小镇逗留的最后一天，作者夫妇做了什么？
questions.a: They took a path out of the town, crossed a few fields, tramped through a dense wood and came to a deep stream, where a boatman ferried them across to a tiny village.
questions.aZh: 他们沿一条出镇的小路穿过几片田地，在密林里跋涉了两个多小时来到一条深溪，由船夫摆渡过溪，到达一个小村庄。
questions.hint: 见 so we decided to spend our last day exploring the countryside 一直到船夫摆渡那几段。

questions.q: What was the only sign of life in the village?
questions.zh: 村里唯一的生命迹象是什么？
questions.a: An ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.
questions.aZh: 附近田里一只面目可憎的黑山羊，被一截短绳拴在一棵树上。
questions.hint: 见 The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being... 一句。

questions.q: How did the children behave when the couple offered them food and spoke to them kindly?
questions.zh: 作者夫妇给孩子们食物、客气地同他们交谈时，孩子们有什么反应？
questions.a: They remained motionless; they just looked at the couple silently as they ate.
questions.aZh: 他们一动不动，只是默不作声地看着夫妇俩吃饭。
questions.hint: 见 We offered them food and spoke to them kindly, but they remained motionless.

questions.q: What does the writer mean by We needed no further warning?
questions.zh: 作者说“我们不需要进一步的警告了”是什么意思？
questions.a: The silent, glaring villagers were themselves the warning: the couple understood at once that they were unwelcome, so they turned back and hurried towards the stream.
questions.aZh: 沉默围观、怒目而视的村民本身就是警告：夫妇俩立刻明白自己不受欢迎，于是转身加快脚步奔向溪边。
questions.hint: 结合上句 There was no doubt that we were unwelcome visitors. 体会。

translation:
在这个旅游频繁的世界上，仍有成千上万个游人足迹未至的地方。
人们总是以为偏僻的地方的村民们热情好客。
但是，那些不但与外国旅游者隔绝，而且与本国同胞隔绝的人们有可能对游客抱有敌意。
到真正偏僻的村庄去旅游并不是一件愉快的事情。
我与妻子在一次周游巴尔干半岛时对此深有体会。
我们在一座小镇上逗留了几天，参观了附近的许多古老的教堂。
这些教堂吸引大量游客，不仅是因为建筑风格奇特，而且还有大量保存完好的壁画。
我们离开小镇的前一天，镇上来了几辆满载游客的公共汽车。
人多得使我们难以忍受，于是我们决定利用最后一天去乡间一游。
我们走上了一条出镇的小路，穿过几块农田，来到一片茂密的树林。
我们原以为小路会到此突然终止。
没想到它到树林中继续向前延伸。
我们在树林中跋涉了两个多小时，到了一条深溪边。
我们可以看到小路在深溪对岸继续向前伸展，但却不知如何越过这道深溪。
突然，妻子发现岸边泊着一条小船，船上有一船夫在呼呼大睡。
我们轻轻地把他唤醒，请他把我们摆渡过溪。
一开始，他很不愿意，但经劝说，终于同意了。
顺着小路，我们来到一个座落在陡峭山坡上的小村庄。
这儿有一条未经修筑的弯弯曲曲的道路，路两边排列着一些矮小的农舍。
农舍全用灰色的土坯建成，因此，即使在晴朗的蓝天底下，村庄看上去也会令人感到难以亲近。
村里似乎无人居住，唯一的生命迹象是附近田里一只面目可憎的黑山羊，用一截短绳拴在一棵树上。
我们在田边一堵东倒西歪的篱笆墙上坐下来，打开几听沙丁鱼罐头，吃了一顿野外午餐。
突然，我注意到妻子十分惊恐。
我抬头一看，发现我们被一群衣衫褴褛的小孩团团围住了，他们在默不作声地看着我们吃饭。
我们给他们东西吃，客客气气地同他们交谈，但他们却一动也不动。
我认为这不过是他们在陌生人面前表现出的害羞。
后来，我们在村里的主要街道上行走的时候，一队默不作声的孩子跟在我们后头。
刚才还似乎空荡荡的村庄一下子活跃了起来，窗口露出了一张张面孔，只穿着衬衣的男人们站在屋子外面凶狠地盯着我们，披黑纱巾的老妇人站在门口偷偷地瞅着我们。
最令人害怕的是到处没有一点声音。
毫无疑问，我们的来访是不受欢迎的。
我们不需要进一步的警告了。
便掉转身子，沿着那条主要街道加快步伐，快速地朝深溪边走去，希望船夫还在那儿等着我们。
title: The Silent Village
subtitle: 沉默的村庄

lead.question: 一对夫妇走进巴尔干半岛的偏僻山村，为何遇上一片令人毛骨悚然的沉默？
lead.warmup: 人们总以为偏远村庄的村民热情好客，作者与妻子却在巴尔干半岛的旅途中发现并非如此。他们离开熙攘的小镇，沿小路穿过树林、渡过深溪，来到一座挂在山坡上的小村。村庄空寂无人，只有一只被拴住的黑山羊。正当他们在破篱笆边野餐时，沉默的人群悄悄围了上来。
goals: 掌握 inaccessible to、hospitable、hostile、straggling、dilapidated、forbidding 等描写偏远村庄的词汇。
读懂 The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being... 这类独立主格结构。
复习被动语态（were built of、were surrounded by、could be heard）以及定语从句和分词短语作定语。
体会全文如何用“沉默”层层渲染紧张气氛，并能依据线索复述故事梗概。
lead.summary: 全文以“沉默”为线索：先写偏僻之地未必好客，再写作者夫妇为躲避游客而深入乡野，历经小路、密林、深溪与渡船，抵达一座灰土坯砌成、看似无人居住的山村。孩子们无声围观、村民从门窗后注视、全村没有一丝声响，最终让他们意识到自己是不受欢迎的不速之客，于是匆匆离去。
lead.tips: 易错提醒：deserted 是形容词“空无一人的”，别与 dessert（甜点）混淆；the only sign of life being... 是独立主格结构，不能写成 is。

exercises.q: 汉译英：在这个旅游频繁的世界上，仍有成千上万个游人足迹未至的地方。
exercises.a: In this much-travelled world, there are still thousands of places which are inaccessible to tourists.

exercises.q: 汉译英：村里似乎无人居住，唯一的生命迹象是附近田里一只面目可憎的黑山羊，用一截短绳拴在一棵树上。
exercises.a: The village seemed deserted, the only sign of life being an ugly-looking black goat on a short length of rope tied to a tree in a field nearby.

exercises.q: 用所给词的正确形式填空：The village seemed ______ (desert), the only sign of life ______ (be) an ugly-looking black goat.
exercises.note: seem后接形容词；独立主格用being。

exercises.q: 改为被动语态：They built all the houses of grey mud bricks.
exercises.a: All the houses were built of grey mud bricks.
exercises.note: 一般过去时被动；be built of。

exercises.q: 改错：Looking up I saw that we surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently.
exercises.a: Looking up I saw that we were surrounded by children in rags who were looking at us silently.

exercises.q: 合并句子（用分词或定语从句）：The path led to a tiny village. It was perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
exercises.a: The path led to a tiny village perched on the steep sides of a mountain.
exercises.note: 过去分词短语作后置定语。

exercises.q: 汉译英：最令人害怕的是到处没有一点声音。
exercises.a: The most frightening thing of all was that not a sound could be heard.
exercises.note: 被动语态；not a sound作主语。

quiz.q: 那座村庄为什么一片沉默？
options: All the villagers had been evacuated before the couple arrived.
The villagers watched the strangers in silence and made no sound at all.
The children were playing a game and had been told not to speak.
The couple were too frightened to speak to anybody.
quiz.note: no sound could be heard，沉默即敌意。

quiz.q: 作者夫妇为什么在最后一天离开小镇去乡间？
options: They wanted to visit more old churches in the vicinity.
They had run out of food and went to buy some in the village.
Several busloads of tourists arrived and it was more than they could bear.
The boatman had invited them to a picnic by the stream.
quiz.note: 游客descended on the town，人多得难以忍受。

quiz.q: The village seemed deserted 中 deserted 最接近的意思是？
options: crowded with noisy visitors
having no people living in it
destroyed by heavy rain
hidden behind a dense wood

quiz.q: 关于那座村庄，下面哪一句符合课文？
options: The houses were built of grey mud bricks and the unmade road straggled along.
The village stood on the flat bank of a deep stream.
The houses were made of stone and contained beautiful frescoes.
The village was famous for its friendly and hospitable inhabitants.

quiz.q: 作者起初怎样解释孩子们的一言不发？
options: He believed they were hungry and wanted his sardines.
He thought they were simply shy of strangers.
He was sure they had come to warn him of danger.
He thought they were the boatman's own children.
quiz.note: I concluded that they were simply shy of strangers.

quiz.q: 夫妇俩走在村里的大街上时，出现了什么情形？
options: The villagers came out and shouted angrily at them.
The village emptied and everybody hid indoors.
Faces appeared at windows, men glared and old women peered, all in silence.
The children led them politely to the boatman's house.
quiz.note: 村庄活跃起来，却仍无一丝声响。
